title: Guest communication, access codes and privacy for short-stay hosts
audience: Hosts and property managers who communicate with short-stay guests and hold access details for their properties.
learningOutcomes: Set out the information a guest needs before arrival and the information they must not receive.
Manage access codes and keys so that each code is limited to the guest and the period it is needed.
Respond to a guest complaint or request through the business's recorded channel.

instruction.heading: What a guest needs, and what they do not
instruction.body: Before arrival, a guest needs the check-in window, how to access the property, the house rules that apply to them, the parking and waste arrangements, and the contact for an emergency. A guest does not need the owner's personal details, the property manager's home address, the access codes for other properties, or the cleaner's rota. Give each guest only what the stay requires. Keep the booking, the guest's contact details and the guest's messages in the business's own recorded channel, so that the record is kept if the host or the staff member changes.

instruction.heading: Access codes and keys
instruction.body: Set each access code to work only for the booking period and to change after each stay. Do not write codes on the property, in a shared public document, or in a message that another guest could see. Record who holds each code and when it was changed. Keys left in a lockbox need a code that is changed after every stay, and the lockbox record must show the date and the person who changed it. If a guest reports that a code does not work, check the booking dates first, then the code, and send a replacement only through the recorded channel.

instruction.heading: Privacy and the guest's information
instruction.body: Collect only the guest information the booking needs, store it where the business's privacy practice says it is stored, and do not share it with a third party without a reason and the business's approval. Do not post a guest's name, photograph or booking details in a public listing, a review reply or a group chat. Where a guest asks what information you hold about them, refer the request to the business owner, who will check the business's obligations for that request. The privacy obligations that apply to a particular business are UNCONFIRMED in this lesson and must be checked for the business.

instruction.heading: Complaints and requests
instruction.body: Answer every complaint or request in the recorded channel, on the same day where possible. Write down the facts: what the guest reported, when, what was checked and what was done. Do not promise a refund, a discount or a compensation amount unless the business owner has set it in writing. Where the complaint concerns a safety issue, such as a gas smell, a broken lock or a damaged electrical fitting, follow the emergency procedure in NEW-HST-04 before replying.

procedure: Send the pre-arrival message through the recorded channel with the check-in window, access arrangements, house rules and emergency contact.
Check that the message contains no owner or property manager personal details and no codes for other properties.
Set the access code to work only for the booking period, and record the date it was set and who set it.
Change the code after the stay, and record the change.
Answer each guest request or complaint in the recorded channel, and write down the facts and the action taken.
Refer any refund, compensation or privacy request to the business owner before replying.

workedExamples.situation: A guest asks for the access code a day before arrival, and the code has not yet been set for their booking.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you send, and when?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not send a code that has not been set for this booking. Check the booking dates and the access record. Set the code for the booking period, then send it through the recorded channel with the check-in window. Record the time it was sent and the person who sent it.

workedExamples.situation: A guest posts the access code for the property in a public review.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do about the code?
workedExamples.reasoning: Change the access code at once, because the old code is no longer private. Record the change and the time. Reply to the review through the business's approved wording, without repeating the code. Tell the business owner, and check any other places the code was shared.

equipmentAndPpe: The business's recorded messaging channel for bookings and guests.
The access record that shows each code, its booking period and the date it was changed.
The emergency contact sheet for the property.

commonErrors.error: Sending access codes by a message that other people can see, or leaving them in a public listing.
commonErrors.prevention: Send codes only to the booking's guest through the recorded channel, and never publish them.

commonErrors.error: Keeping one access code for a property across many bookings.
commonErrors.prevention: Set a new code for each booking period and change it after each stay.

commonErrors.error: Answering a complaint by phone or a private message only, with no record.
commonErrors.prevention: Reply in the recorded channel and write down the facts and the action.

commonErrors.error: Promising a refund or compensation without the owner's approval.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer any money-related request to the business owner.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Privacy obligations for collecting, storing and disclosing guest information depend on the business's size, its activities and the place where it operates. They are UNCONFIRMED in this lesson. Flagged for expert review.
A guest who reports a safety problem, such as a gas smell or an electrical fault, must be directed to the emergency procedure before any routine reply. Emergency procedure is set out in NEW-HST-04.
This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate or authority to deal with guest data, complaints or disputes on behalf of an owner.

qualityStandard: Every pre-arrival message contains the required information and no personal details of the owner or other properties.
Every access code is limited to its booking period and changed after the stay.
Every guest complaint or request has a recorded reply and a record of the action taken.
documentationEvidence: Copy of the pre-arrival message sent through the recorded channel.
Access record with the code's booking period, the date set and the date changed.
Complaint or request record with the facts, the reply and the action taken.
summary: Give each guest only the information the stay requires.
Limit each access code to its booking period and change it after the stay.
Record every guest communication, and refer refunds and privacy requests to the owner.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which information belongs in a pre-arrival message to a guest?
options: The owner's home address and phone number
The check-in window, access arrangements, house rules and emergency contact
The access codes for the other properties on the same street

knowledgeChecks.question: A guest's access code has been posted publicly. What is the first step?
options: Wait until the guest checks out
Change the access code at once and record the change
Ask the guest to delete the post

knowledgeChecks.question: A guest asks for a refund for a noisy neighbour. Who decides on the money?
options: The business owner, against a written approval
